units.text: # reBot B601-DM

[reBot B601-DM](⟦0⟧) is an open-source, low-cost robot arm from Seeed Studio for embodied-AI and imitation learning. It comes as a **follower** arm (the ⟦1⟧, a 6-DOF arm plus gripper driven by Damiao CAN motors) and a **leader** arm (the ⟦2⟧ / ⟦3⟧, driven by FashionStar UART smart servos) used to teleoperate it.
This page covers **calibration** and **teleoperation** for both single-arm and bimanual (dual-arm) setups.
_Left: the B601-DM follower at its zero position. Right: the reBot Arm 102 leader at its zero position. Images courtesy of [Seeed Studio](⟦0⟧)._
## Install LeRobot 🤗
Follow our [Installation Guide](⟦0⟧), then install the reBot support:
This pulls in ⟦0⟧ (CAN motor control for the B601-DM follower) and ⟦1⟧ (FashionStar UART servos for the reBot Arm 102 leader).
## Registered device types
| Type                     | Kind                                         |
| ⟦0⟧    | single-arm B601-DM follower robot            |
| ⟦0⟧ | bimanual (dual-arm) follower robot           |
| ⟦0⟧       | single-arm reBot Arm 102 leader teleoperator |
| ⟦0⟧    | bimanual (dual-arm) leader teleoperator      |

The bimanual types compose two single-arm instances and namespace each arm's
observation/action keys with a ⟦0⟧ / ⟦1⟧ prefix. Per-arm settings are
passed through nested ⟦2⟧ / ⟦3⟧ arguments.
## Find the USB ports
For each device, find the USB port associated with its motor bus using:

⟦0⟧
  On Linux, remove ⟦1⟧ (⟦2⟧) so it does not hold the
  leader's USB serial port. You may also need to grant access to the serial
  devices: ⟦3⟧.
## Calibration

Neither arm stores a persistent hardware calibration: every time it connects, the motors are re-zeroed against the pose the arm is physically holding. Calibration simply records that zero pose. When prompted, **manually move the arm to its zero position** (the default sit-down pose shown above, gripper fully closed) and press ⟦0⟧.
### Follower (B601-DM)
Connect the bimanual follower; calibration runs for the left arm, then the right arm.
Per-arm calibration files are saved with ⟦0⟧ / ⟦1⟧ suffixes on the id.
### Leader (reBot Arm 102)
## Teleoperation

Once both arms are calibrated, drive the follower with the leader. The follower talks to its CAN bus through a Damiao serial bridge (⟦0⟧, the default) or a SocketCAN adapter (⟦1⟧). See the [OpenArm page](⟦2⟧) for more details on the SocketCAN adapter configuration.

The bimanual leader and follower reuse the single-arm classes; each arm is
configured through nested ⟦0⟧ / ⟦1⟧ arguments,
so a bimanual reBot Arm 102 leader drives a bimanual B601-DM follower.

⟦0⟧
  The leader and follower share the same joint names (`shoulder_pan,
  shoulder_lift, elbow_flex, wrist_flex, wrist_yaw, wrist_roll, gripper`), so
  leader actions map directly onto the follower.
If the motion of a joint is reversed, flip its sign in the leader's ⟦0⟧ (the gripper also carries a scale to widen its range to the follower):
## Recording datasets
Swap ⟦0⟧ for ⟦1⟧ (with the same ⟦2⟧ / ⟦3⟧ arguments, plus ⟦4⟧) to record demonstrations for training. See [Imitation Learning for Robots](⟦5⟧) for the full workflow.
For hardware assembly and wiring, see the [Seeed Studio reBot wiki](⟦0⟧).
